title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 63
paragraphs: The Athenians did as they were told, and so Peisistratus for the third time gained possession of Athens, and he firmly rooted his tyranny by means of many foreign mercenaries and much revenue of money, coming partly from the land itself and partly from the region of the river Strymon. He also took as hostages the sons of those Athenians who had remained in the land and had not at once fled, and placed them in the hands of Naxos; for Peisistratus had also conquered this island by war and had handed it over to the charge of Lygdamis. Moreover, besides this, he purified the island of Delos in obedience to the oracles, and his purification was of this kind: so far as the view from the temple extended, he dug up all the dead bodies that were buried in that part and removed them to another part of Delos. So Peisistratus was tyrant of the Athenians; but of the Athenians some had fallen in the battle, while others, along with the sons of Alcmaeon, were exiles from their native land.
